solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Futile hope to be taken by tube about a mile

blocks.note: something piped is carried along a pipe or tube
re means about or concerning
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: Someone hopes in vain to catch the Underground a mile away.
explanation.walkthrough: A pipe dream was originally the fantasy of an opium smoker, which fits the tube in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is an unrealistic wish that will never come true, so it is a hope without any prospect.

clue.text: Samuel shows energy, indeed to extremes

indicators.note: going only to the extremes means just the two end letters of the word survive

blocks.note: pep is vigour or energy
yes, as an emphatic indeed

explanation.surface: Someone named Samuel is shown to be energetic to an extreme degree.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the outer letters of YES are kept, giving YS. Samuel Pepys was the 17th-century English diarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys is the famous diarist, so his first name stands as an example clue for the surname.

clue.text: Possible spin doctor runs into office in exhausted collapse

indicators.note: one thing running into another ends up inside it

blocks.note: a PRO is a public relations officer, which a spin doctor might be
a station is a post or position held
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A worn-out PR man bursts into the office and collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' signals that a spin doctor is only one kind of public relations officer. Station here is the old sense of one's post or rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostration is complete physical exhaustion, a state of collapse from fatigue or heat.

clue.text: Daughter spilled petrol, the tiniest amount

indicators.note: spilled liquid splashes everywhere, so its letters end up scattered in a new order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter at the pump spills only a drop of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet is a very small drop of liquid, so it means a minute quantity.

clue.text: At country club piano, arrangement for choir really delighted

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks a piece, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: the European Union is a club of countries
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A choir is thrilled with a new piano arrangement performed at a country club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' looks like a golf club; it is the European Union, a club of nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoric means feeling intense happiness or elation, matching very delighted.

clue.text: What's making two women sick?

blocks.note: ma is mother, a woman
a lady is the second woman

explanation.surface: A question about what has made a pair of women ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The two women are MA and LADY joined; the whole clue then asks what is making someone sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or disease, the thing that makes a person sick.

clue.text: Governor gets aide to admit the result of smoking

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant
ash is what is left after smoking

explanation.surface: A governor has his assistant let in some cigarette ash.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman official, often a provincial governor.

clue.text: Criticise expert answer: will that fix everything?

blocks.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
an ace is an expert
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone scorns an expert's answer, doubting it will solve every problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is phrased as a doubtful question, hinting at a supposed cure for all ills.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a remedy claimed to cure every ailment or solve every problem.

clue.text: Old coin not enough for a bowl at lunchtime?

indicators.note: not enough suggests falling short, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: soup is typically served in a bowl at lunch

explanation.surface: A small change coin would not buy a bowl of lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUP loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sou was a French coin of low value, no longer in use.

clue.text: One relatively friendly target?

blocks.note: surface reading: a target that is fairly amiable
setter's reading: a relative (a parent's sister) who is friendly, given a girl's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean 'fairly', but it points to a family relation, the aunt; the named target is a pub game and a byword for someone everyone attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally is a figure thrown at in a fairground game, hence any person or idea that attracts criticism.

clue.text: A means of advertising for a very short time

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
mo is short for moment

explanation.surface: An advert designed to run only very briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a promotional piece such as a trailer or advert used to publicise something.

clue.text: Arrange to keep a single one of several newborns in litter

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

blocks.note: to plan is to arrange
taken as written
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: Someone arranges to keep one newborn from a large litter of puppies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like a set of newborn animals, but it is the old sense of a couch carried on poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A palanquin is a covered seat carried on poles, the same thing as a litter for transporting people.

clue.text: Eldest child originally rootless, out to take revenge

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is used
out suggests being put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eldest child, uprooted and adrift, sets out to get even.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle old scores is an idiom for getting revenge for past wrongs.

clue.text: Music which receives honour about to upset colleagues?

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
something that receives another takes it inside

blocks.note: rock is a genre of music
that as a relative pronoun, meaning which
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A rock musician given an honour causes trouble among bandmates.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is figurative: nobody's boat is literally rocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock the boat is an idiom meaning to cause disruption in a group, unsettling those you work with.

clue.text: What has insect got into? Obvious: a fruit

indicators.note: the question asks what one word has got into another, so it sits inside

blocks.note: plain means clear or obvious
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what bug has crawled into the fruit; the answer is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'What has insect got into?' is itself the container instruction, with 'Obvious' as the host.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy fruit of the banana family, usually cooked before eating.

clue.text: Very important charge raised over a pile up

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a rap is a criminal charge
taken as written
to mount up is to accumulate

explanation.surface: An urgent charge is brought about a heap that has built up.
explanation.walkthrough: RAP reversed is PAR; 'over' places it above the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or of the highest importance.

clue.text: A measure of pressure has rogue initially taking two steps back

indicators.note: the first letter moves back two places in the alphabet, swapping it for another

blocks.note: a rascal is a rogue

explanation.surface: A rogue backs off two paces under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: R stepped back two letters in the alphabet (R, Q, P) becomes P.
explanation.definitionFit: The pascal is the SI unit of pressure, one newton per square metre.

clue.text: Scoundrel charges for borrowing draughts

blocks.note: a cur is a contemptible man
rents are payments for using something

explanation.surface: A rogue charges people to borrow a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draughts' suggests the board game (checkers); here it is flows of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Currents of air through a room are draughts, flows of cold air.

clue.text: Picked up and pulled down by the ears

indicators.note: judged by the ears means only the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: first meaning: lifted
second meaning, by sound: demolished

explanation.surface: Something lifted and then dragged down by its ears.
explanation.walkthrough: One spelling means lifted; a word that sounds the same, razed, means demolished.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised means lifted up, and razed, its sound-alike, means levelled to the ground.

clue.text: Work of art attractive but lacking force

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: fetching means attractive
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A piece of art that is pretty but lacks power.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from a plate incised with acid, a recognised art form.

clue.text: Back at university, go on course that may have strings attached

indicators.note: going back means reading in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, an Oxford degree course
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A student returning to college takes a course whose funding has conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' is British usage for being at university, and 'on' in an across clue puts the attempt after the course. 'Strings attached' sounds like a conditional deal but means marionette strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Puppetry is the art of working puppets, and marionettes are worked by strings.

clue.text: Scuttle round minister to get accepted

indicators.note: going round something encloses it

blocks.note: a scuttle is a coal bucket, a kind of pail
Rev is short for Reverend, a minister of religion

explanation.surface: Someone scurries around a clergyman to win his approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scuttle' looks like a verb, to hurry; it is the noun, a coal scuttle, a bucket for carrying coal.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win out or become generally established, as a view that gains acceptance.

clue.text: Unstable element so long emitting energy in empty room

indicators.note: emitting means giving off, so a letter is let out
in means placed within the other piece
emptied of its middle, a word leaves only its outer letters

blocks.note: adieu is a farewell
E is the symbol for energy
outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A radioactive element has long been giving off energy in a vacant room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' reads as a length of time but is a farewell; only one of its two E's is let go.
explanation.definitionFit: Radium is a radioactive chemical element, its nuclei unstable and decaying.

clue.text: Example of appeasement of menace hurting me badly

indicators.note: badly means wrongly made, so these letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Giving in to a threat ends up hurting the person doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fair judgement on the 1938 pact itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1938 Munich Agreement, ceding the Sudetenland to Hitler, is the classic case of appeasing an aggressor.

clue.text: Herb's two pronouns

blocks.note: thy is the old possessive pronoun for you
me is the first-person object pronoun

explanation.surface: A man called Herb has two pronouns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name; it is the plant, with 's as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic plant used to flavour cooking, a culinary herb.

clue.text: After British downfall, Scotsman becomes European

indicators.note: after places the following pieces later in the line

blocks.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British
rain falls down
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman takes a new nationality after Britain's decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' suggests ruin; read literally it is something that falls down.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ukrainian is someone from Ukraine, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Port found in poor Spanish-speaking area with no bar

indicators.note: with no means without, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: a barrio is a Spanish-speaking district, often poor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A port is found in a poor Hispanic district that has no pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian seaport, known simply as Rio.

clue.text: Leave in some considerable pain

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: any as in some amount
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone departs while in a lot of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme physical or mental suffering.

clue.text: Beachwear at first rather lost in the crowd

indicators.note: at first points to the opening, so only the initial letter is used
something lost is gone, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: first letter of the word
a throng is a crowd

explanation.surface: Skimpy swimwear that at first seems rather lost among the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: THRONG loses R, from 'at first rather'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy swimsuit or bikini bottom worn on the beach.

clue.text: We hear a girl will pull, which encourages a kiss?

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the words are spelt differently

blocks.note: a miss is a girl; will is shortened to 'll; to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: A girl who will try to pull someone, with a kiss as the lure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' sounds like slang for picking someone up romantically; here it is to tow. People kiss under mistletoe at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition says people meeting under mistletoe at Christmas should kiss.
